content.title: About
content.content: Egg roll, meatless is a vegetarian roll snack made from rice paper, vegetables, tofu and aromatic spices. It has a crispy outer layer and a tender filling that mimics a traditional egg roll without meat or eggs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vegetarian version is popular in Asian cuisine as a meat‑free alternative.
To achieve a crunchy crust, rolls are often deep‑fried at 180 °C for 2–3 minutes.
Tofu in the filling provides plant‑based protein and makes the dish more filling.
A blend of soy sauce, ginger and garlic gives the roll its characteristic savory flavor.
Egg roll, meatless is commonly served with sweet chili sauce or soy sauce.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Tofu and vegetables supply a good amount of protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Absence of meat and eggs makes the roll less fatty than traditional versions.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Carrots, cabbage and peppers contain vitamins B6 and B9, important for metabolism.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Cabbage and carrots aid digestion and promote satiety.

items.title: Low cholesterol
items.content: No animal products means the dish is suitable for cholesterol‑lowering diets.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Tofu may trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to soy.

items.title: High sodium in sauces
items.content: Soy sauce and ready‑made seasonings can increase salt intake; choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Trans fats from frying
items.content: Frequent deep‑frying can generate trans fats; limit the number of fried rolls.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Improper storage or reheating may lead to bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Egg roll, meatless can be enjoyed hot as a snack, served with soy sauce, sweet chili or ginger dipping sauce. Slice into bite‑size pieces for appetizers or as a side to a main dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked rolls in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in the oven or skillet to restore crispness. Freezing is not recommended as the wrapper loses its texture.
